title: Agreements that at least doubled through amendments
question: Which City agreements grew far beyond their first approved amount by being amended, without a new award?
finding: 159 agreements at least doubled and grew by $10 million or more through amendments the Board approved from 2014 to 2026; 23 grew five times or more. 80 of the 159 began between $9 million and $10 million, just under the amount at which the Board must approve a contract, and now stand at $2.97 billion together. 63 are with profiled nonprofits and 141 are with payees that carry other warning signs on this site.
how: Board of Supervisors titles were linked into chains. Only links proven by a dollar figure carried from one title to the next, or by a shared contract number, are followed. The first amount is the earliest stated total (or the "from" amount of the first amendment, which is how an agreement first signed below $10 million shows up); the latest is the highest total approved. Grant acceptances and legal settlements are left out.
limits: Each step was approved in a public vote. Many contracts are written with options to extend, and costs rise with demand. The titles do not say whether the work was offered to anyone else before it was extended, so this screen shows growth, not that competition was skipped. An agreement that never crosses the Board's $10 million threshold never appears. Emergency work (pandemic testing, hotel rooms, meals) explains several of the steepest rises in 2020 and 2021.
